subject: Literature
title: North Korea's Total Information Control
description: A micro-lesson that makes North Korea's Total Information Control usable.

hook.text: In North Korea, possessing a foreign novel can result in public execution, making it the world's most censored country.

buildup.text: Citizens may only access books approved by the state, and all literature must glorify the ruling Kim dynasty.

discovery.text: Defectors report that smuggled USB drives containing South Korean dramas and novels are changing minds from within.

twist.text: The regime considers foreign stories so dangerous that it passed a law in 2020 punishing their distribution with death.

climax.text: North Korea demonstrates that total censorship requires total control, and even one smuggled story threatens the system.

punchline.text: A regime that fears a USB drive fears its own fragility.

quiz.question: Why does North Korea consider foreign stories extremely dangerous?
options: Even one smuggled story can challenge the regime's total information control
They are written in languages citizens cannot read
